1//! Serde Integration for InfluxDB. Provides deserialization of query returns.
2//!
3//! When querying multiple series in the same query (e.g. with a regex query), it might be desirable to flat map
4//! the resulting series into a single `Vec` like so. The example assumes, that there are weather readings in multiple
5//! series named `weather_<city_name>` (e.g. `weather_berlin`, or `weather_london`). Since we're using a Regex query,
6//! we don't actually know which series will be returned. To assign the city name to the series, we can use the series
7//! `name`, InfluxDB provides alongside query results.
8//!
9//! ```rust,no_run
10//! use influxdb::{Client, Query as _, ReadQuery};
11//! use serde_derive::Deserialize;
12//!
13//! #[derive(Deserialize)]
14//! struct WeatherWithoutCityName {
15//!     temperature: i32,
16//! }
17//!
18//! #[derive(Deserialize)]
19//! struct Weather {
20//!     city_name: String,
21//!     weather: WeatherWithoutCityName,
22//! }
23//!
24//! # #[tokio::main]
25//! # async fn main() -> Result<(), influxdb::Error> {
26//! let client = Client::new("http://localhost:8086", "test");
27//! let query = ReadQuery::new(
28//!     "SELECT temperature FROM /weather_[a-z]*$/ WHERE time > now() - 1m ORDER BY DESC",
29//! );
30//! let mut db_result = client.json_query(query).await?;
31//! let _result = db_result
32//!     .deserialize_next::<WeatherWithoutCityName>()?
33//!     .series
34//!     .into_iter()
35//!     .map(|mut city_series| {
36//!         let city_name = city_series.name.split("_").collect::<Vec<&str>>().remove(2);
37//!         Weather {
38//!             weather: city_series.values.remove(0),
39//!             city_name: city_name.to_string(),
40//!         }
41//!     })
42//!     .collect::<Vec<Weather>>();
43//! # Ok(())
44//! # }
45//! ```
46
47mod de;

49use serde::de::DeserializeOwned;
50use serde_derive::Deserialize;
51
52use crate::client::check_status;
53use crate::{Client, Error, Query, ReadQuery};
54
55#[derive(Deserialize)]
56#[doc(hidden)]
57struct _DatabaseError {
58    error: String,
59}
60
61#[derive(Deserialize, Debug)]
62#[doc(hidden)]
63pub struct DatabaseQueryResult {
64    pub results: Vec<serde_json::Value>,
65}
66
67impl DatabaseQueryResult {
68    pub fn deserialize_next<T: 'static>(&mut self) -> Result<Return<T>, Error>
69    where
70        T: DeserializeOwned + Send,
71    {
72        serde_json::from_value::<Return<T>>(self.results.remove(0)).map_err(|err| {
73            Error::DeserializationError {
74                error: format!("could not deserialize: {err}"),
75            }
76        })
77    }
78
79    pub fn deserialize_next_tagged<TAG, T: 'static>(
80        &mut self,
81    ) -> Result<TaggedReturn<TAG, T>, Error>
82    where
83        TAG: DeserializeOwned + Send,
84        T: DeserializeOwned + Send,
85    {
86        serde_json::from_value::<TaggedReturn<TAG, T>>(self.results.remove(0)).map_err(|err| {
87            Error::DeserializationError {
88                error: format!("could not deserialize: {err}"),
89            }
90        })
91    }
92}

94#[derive(Deserialize, Debug)]
95#[doc(hidden)]
96pub struct Return<T> {
97    #[serde(default = "Vec::new")]
98    pub series: Vec<Series<T>>,
99}

101#[derive(Debug)]
102/// Represents a returned series from InfluxDB
103pub struct Series<T> {
104    pub name: String,
105    pub values: Vec<T>,
106}

108#[derive(Deserialize, Debug)]
109#[doc(hidden)]
110pub struct TaggedReturn<TAG, T> {
111    #[serde(default = "Vec::new")]
112    pub series: Vec<TaggedSeries<TAG, T>>,
113}

115#[derive(Debug)]
116/// Represents a returned series from InfluxDB
117pub struct TaggedSeries<TAG, T> {
118    pub name: String,
119    pub tags: TAG,
120    pub values: Vec<T>,
121}

123impl Client {
124    pub async fn json_query(&self, q: ReadQuery) -> Result<DatabaseQueryResult, Error> {
125        let query = q.build().map_err(|err| Error::InvalidQueryError {
126            error: err.to_string(),
127        })?;
128
129        let read_query = query.get();
130        let read_query_lower = read_query.to_lowercase();
131
132        if !read_query_lower.contains("select") && !read_query_lower.contains("show") {
133            let error = Error::InvalidQueryError {
134                error: "Only SELECT and SHOW queries supported with JSON deserialization".into(),
135            };
136            return Err(error);
137        }
138
139        let url = &format!("{}/query", &self.url);
140        let mut parameters = self.parameters.as_ref().clone();
141        parameters.insert("q", read_query);
142        let mut request_builder = self.client.get(url);
143        if let Some(ref token) = self.token {
144            request_builder = request_builder.header("Authorization", format!("Token {token}"))
145        }
146        let request_builder = request_builder.query(&parameters);
147
148        let res = request_builder
149            .send()
150            .await
151            .map_err(|err| Error::ConnectionError {
152                error: err.to_string(),
153            })?;
154        check_status(&res)?;
155
156        let body = res.bytes();
157
158        let body = body.await.map_err(|err| Error::ProtocolError {
159            error: err.to_string(),
160        })?;
161
162        // Try parsing InfluxDBs { "error": "error message here" }
163        if let Ok(error) = serde_json::from_slice::<_DatabaseError>(&body) {
164            return Err(Error::DatabaseError { error: error.error });
165        }
166
167        // Json has another structure, let's try actually parsing it to the type we're deserializing
168        serde_json::from_slice::<DatabaseQueryResult>(&body).map_err(|err| {
169            Error::DeserializationError {
170                error: format!("serde error: {err}"),
171            }
172        })
173    }
174}
